summary: Compaction can irreversibly omit an invariant, amplify a mistaken interpretation across generations of summaries, or make relevant evidence unreachable through a poor retrieval key.

points.text: A summary may drop a rare exception or negative requirement precisely because it looked unimportant before the later task made it decisive.
Repeatedly summarizing prior summaries creates semantic drift and laundering: unsupported inferences become compacted facts that later models no longer question.
Just-in-time retrieval fails when filenames change, indexes lag, embeddings miss exact constraints, or the compact frame no longer contains the term needed to formulate the query.
Compression and retrieval add calls, latency, state management, and privacy exposure; short, well-scoped tasks may perform better with a deliberately small original context.
